newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-HAYDEN LEADS AUSTRALIAN RUN FEAST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HAYDEN LEADS AUSTRALIAN RUN FEAST.

text.p: Matthew Hayden slammed a rapid 112 as Australian romped to 439 for four on the first day of their tour opening three-day match against South African champions Western Province at Newlands on Saturday.

The 25-year-old left hander showed scant respect for the home team's all-international bowling attack and repeatedly dispatched a plethora of short-pitched deliveries to the mid-wicket and square-leg boundaries.

Hayden's innings spanned 177 deliveries and contained 14 boundaries but of even more significance was the return to form of captain Mark Taylor who put a home summer of miserable form behind him with 85 in an opening stand of 194 with Hayden.
It was Taylor's first half-century for 15 innings, nine of them in tests against the West Indies, and he clearly grew in confidence and stature after an awkward start.
Having unselfishly fed the strike to the dominant Hayden, Taylor reached 50 an hour after his partner from 86 balls, just 12 more than Hayden.

Hayden eventually departed after splicing the umpteenth Brett Schultz bouncer to extra cover and Taylor followed soon after, edging the last ball before tea from Meyrick Pringle to wicketkeeper Mario Solomons. His 85 came from 140 balls with 10 fours.

An already high scoring tempo increased further with the arrival of Matthew Elliott and Steve Waugh at the crease. Elliott hit two hooked sixes in one over from Schultz and went on to make 74 sparkling runs which also included 10 fours from just 88 deliveries.
He departed to a catch on the deep square-leg boundary attempting another six.

Waugh made his customary cautious start before blossoming with a series of imperious straight and cover drives to reach 69 from 102 balls with 12 spanking fours. He, like all his team mates, departed to an attacking shot, caught at cover.

As the home side bowling withered under the onslaught, the over rate slowed to ridiculous proportions and the floodlights had to be turned on for the final two hours to continue play which finally ended 70 minutes after the scheduled close.
Greg Blewett showed no sympathy for the shell-shocked bowlers and continued the punishment with an aggressive 48 not out.
